memory_update.text: FORM should be tracked as a direct HBM test-interface candidate; key validation is HBM-specific probe-card revenue, customer concentration, and margin contribution.
CAMT should be tracked as an advanced-packaging and HBM inspection/metrology candidate; verify revenue mix and customer concentration before promoting beyond Layer 1.
ONTO is a larger-cap but still specialized process-control candidate for HBM and advanced packaging; keep as an underfollowed-quality comparator rather than a pure small-cap discovery name.
KLIC is a lower-attention hypothesis around thermocompression bonding and AI advanced packaging; requires stronger evidence on materiality and HBM-specific demand.

For the HBM upstream-input node, the most actionable US-listed sub-layers found in this pass are probe/test, inspection/metrology, and advanced bonding equipment rather than the HBM producers themselves.

Still need a separate materials/chemicals pass for underfill, bonding films, substrates, thermal interface materials, specialty gases, and ultra-pure chemicals; US-listed pure plays may be harder to identify and may sit inside diversified suppliers.

summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for HBM and advanced-packaging upstream inputs with a two-lane structure. Reference context remains HBM producers, TSMC/CoWoS, and AI accelerator customers, but this pass prioritizes smaller or niche equipment/test/inspection suppliers where HBM growth creates qualification-gated demand. The strongest candidates in this pass are probe-card/test interface, inspection/metrology, and thermocompression/advanced-packaging assembly equipment vendors. No buy/sell recommendation is implied.
